Description: Mass (mg) of solid material digested or volume (mL) of liquid taken for dissolution.

Total number of distinct acid digestion steps required to dissolve the sample. Some procedures require multiple sequential steps — for example, an initial open-beaker HF–HNO3 dissolution followed by a second closed-vessel step for residues retaining refractory minerals, or by an aqua regia reflux to destroy fluoride complexes.
Type of vessel used for acid digestion.
Acid mixture used for sample dissolution. Record acid type(s) and concentration(s) where known (e.g., concentrated HF–HNO3 in Parr bombs is standard for silicate dissolution).
Temperature at which acid digestion was carried out (°C). Procedure specifies the target temperature.
Duration of the primary acid digestion step (hours or days).

Whether chromatographic separation of element groups (e.g., using ion exchange resin) was performed prior to analysis. Record resin type and elution matrix conditions if applied. Record 'None' if the direct digestion solution is analyzed.

Isotopic spike material added to the sample before or during digestion for isotope dilution (ID) analysis or double-spike mass bias correction. For double-spike procedures, the spike must be added and equilibrated before digestion to correct for any isotopic fractionation during dissolution and column chemistry. For concentration ID, the spike must be added before digestion for complete equilibration. Record spike name or certificate reference, spike isotopes, and whether added pre- or post-digestion. Record 'None' if ID or double-spike technique is not used.

Acid type and concentration of the final dissolved sample solution introduced to the instrument. For isotope-ratio procedures, acid molarity must be precisely matched between samples and bracketing standards to avoid matrix-induced mass bias offsets. Procedures targeting HFSE may add trace HF to the final solution to keep those elements in solution.
Type and material of the pneumatic nebulizer used for sample introduction.

Description: Type of spray chamber and cooling temperature if thermostatted (°C).
Desolvating nebulizer or membrane desolvator used upstream of the plasma to reduce solvent load. Record 'None' if not used.
Peristaltic pump speed or self-aspiration flow rate for sample introduction (µL/min or mL/min).
Flow rate of the carrier argon gas delivered through the nebulizer (L/min). Adjusted daily to optimize signal.
Duration of instrument rinse between successive sample solutions (seconds).
Target concentration of internal standard element(s) in all measured solutions (µg/L or ppb). Record 'N/A' where Internal Standard Element is 'None'.
